headline: Iran faces choice between deal and 'devastation'
dek: Hegseth: 'Iran's going to have a choice to make real quick about whether they're going to give those up at the table or face the kind of devastation that America can bring and will bring swiftly if necessary' — referring to Iran's 'nuclear ambitions.' Accused Tehran of building a large…
sources: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking to ROTC cadets and military recruits at the University of Tennessee (via Anadolu Agency; carried by TRT World, Saudi Gazette, Dawn, TimesNow liveblog)
fault_line: Is 'devastation' the stick that forces Tehran to the table — or campaign-season theater while the blockade does the real work?

sections.what_happened: Hegseth: 'Iran's going to have a choice to make real quick about whether they're going to give those up at the table or face the kind of devastation that America can bring and will bring swiftly if necessary' — referring to Iran's 'nuclear ambitions.' Accused Tehran of building a large conventional missile arsenal to deter military action while pursuing nuclear ambitions; accused Iran of funding 'the proxies in Hezbollah' and 'the proxies in the Ansar Allah in Yemen'; said Washington sought to deter attacks on US forces and shipping. Framed Iran policy as part of Trump's broader reassertion of US power (drug cartels; limiting Iranian/Chinese/Russian influence in Latin America); said the US Venezuela operation would have 'generational implications.'
sections.what_verified: AA, TRT World, Saudi Gazette, Dawn, vietnam.vn, TimesNow liveblog carry identical quotes; consistent with Trump's Friday 'considering limited strikes' posture (0200-01)
sections.what_disputed: Rhetoric, not policy: no new strike authorization announced; contradicts Trump's Oct 8 'no strikes before midterms' pledge in tone but not in letter; Iran's position (Baqaei, Araghchi) is readiness for diplomacy 'as much as war'
sections.why_matters: The Pentagon chief said the quiet part on a college stage: negotiate or be devastated. Pair the quote card with the asymmetry — Trump's 'no strikes before midterms' pledge vs his own defense secretary's 'swiftly if necessary.' The fault line is the gap between the words and the war.
sections.context: Background: US/Iran — NEW (missed by prior scans): Defense Secretary Hegseth at Tennessee ROTC — Iran faces choice between deal and 'devastation'; accuses Tehran of proxy funding

totw_analysis: Our read: The Pentagon chief said the quiet part on a college stage: negotiate or be devastated. Pair the quote card with the asymmetry — Trump's 'no strikes before midterms' pledge vs his own defense secretary's 'swiftly if necessary.' The fault line is the gap between the words and the war. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is 'devastation' the stick that forces Tehran to the table — or campaign-season theater while the blockade does the real work?
